decisions.statement: A turn asks the attempt handed in for one run at the pool.
An attempt that served a response answers with that response.
An attempt that served a response reads no pacing.
An attempt that found no account reads the pacing of every account.
The step a turn takes is decided by `queue-step`.
A wait step sleeps the span that step names.
A wait step adds the span slept to the silent elapsed.
A wait step is followed by another attempt.
A commit step answers with the committed keepalive the caller handed in.
A commit step tells that keepalive why the pool was empty.
An exhaust step answers with the rate-limit response the caller handed in.
An exhaust step tells that response the pool summary and the moment of the turn.
The turn ceiling here is 32 turns.
A queued request takes at most the turns the turn ceiling names.
A request reaching the turn ceiling throws rather than answering with a response.
A request reaching the turn ceiling is written about before the throw.
The turn ceiling sits above the turns the silent budget can produce.
A turn-ceiling line names the turns the ceiling allowed.
The client stream flag is read off the body bytes before the first attempt.
The client stream flag is read the once for a whole request.
A wait line names the span waited and the silent elapsed.
A commit line names how every account is placed against its limits.
An exhaust line names the eligible count against the total.
An earliest reset that is absent is written as `unknown`.
How the accounts are placed is worked out only where a turn commits or exhausts.
Every line names the account trail the attempt answered with.
The clock is handed in so a test needs no real time.
The sleep is handed in so a test needs no wait.
Every line written here goes to a door the caller may replace.
A caller hands in the attempt one turn is made of.
A caller hands in the response a committed request is served with.
A caller hands in the response an exhausted pool is refused with.
A caller may name a turn ceiling tighter than the ceiling named here.
Nothing here reads a page.
Nothing here chooses an account.
Nothing here forwards a request.
Nothing here has a clock the caller cannot replace.
The pacing of every account is read again on every turn.
A turn ceiling reached is answered 502 by the handler rather than named to the client.
A line saying how the accounts are placed grows with the accounts filed.
An attempt that throws is thrown on to the caller unwritten about.
The silent budget and the hold horizon are read off `queue-step` rather than handed in.
Nothing here proves this loop against the pick pipeline the caller hands in.
The moment of the turn is read before the pacing rather than after.

definition: the re-probing a request waits through when no account is eligible to have that request
